# Design

How this app is built: its stack, layout and conventions.
Read it with `AGENTS.md`, which has the working rules and how the app is tested.

*TanStack's own documentation is vendored in this repo under `docs/tanstack/`: the official
`llms.txt` index for TanStack Router (`router.llms.txt`) and TanStack Query (`query.llms.txt`).
Consult it when working with TanStack Router or Query.*

---

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints — routes MUST live under `rest/api/`

Put every domain REST route under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/` so its path starts
with `/api/`: `SpaConfig` only lets `/api/*` reach the backend, and a non-`/api/` route is swallowed
by the SPA deep-link fallback (it returns `index.html`, not your endpoint). The reference below uses
non-`/api/` example paths for brevity — in this app the `/api/` prefix is required. See
`src/main/resources/officefloor/README.md`.

---

*The following is OfficeFloor's own agent guidance for this stack, included verbatim
from <https://officefloor.net/AGENTS.md>. It is part of the OfficeFloor architecture.*

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints

Applies when adding or changing REST endpoints. This project serves REST through
OfficeFloor Function Injection, **not** Spring MVC controllers: each endpoint is a
pipeline of small function classes wired together in YAML.

- Requires the OfficeFloor Spring Boot starter in the build:
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter` (Spring Boot 4.x) or
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-3-starter` (Spring Boot 3.x). Without it these YAML
  files are inert. (Rules below track these starter versions.)
- Define each endpoint as a YAML file under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/`,
  named `<path>.<METHOD>.yml` (e.g. `owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml` → `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`).
- One small function class per step; compose steps with `next:` and `outputs:`.
- Do NOT generate `@RestController`, `@GetMapping` or `@PostMapping`.

-- Who holds a claim's editor open (the user who pressed its edit button), so no one else can open it until it is
-- saved or cancelled or the sheet's today changes. Null when no one does.
ALTER TABLE claim ADD COLUMN locked_by VARCHAR(200);
-- The screen can show a sheet as it stood at the end of a date (an as-of view): every change made while the sheet's
-- today was on or before it counts, every later one does not. These keep the sheet's today when each change was made
-- (null: made before this was kept; there from the beginning).

-- The sheet's today when it was archived.
ALTER TABLE sheet_archived ADD COLUMN archived_on DATE;

-- The sheet's today when the period was added.
ALTER TABLE period ADD COLUMN added_on DATE;

-- Every close, soft close and reopen of a period, in the order made, with the figures it fixed: total is the
-- period's due-total, person_totals each person's as "personId=total" joined by ";" (both null on a reopen).
CREATE TABLE period_log (
    id            BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    sheet_id      VARCHAR(200)  NOT NULL,
    period_id     BIGINT        NOT NULL,
    closed        BOOLEAN       NOT NULL,
    soft_closed   BOOLEAN       NOT NULL,
    closed_total  DECIMAL(12, 2),
    person_totals VARCHAR(8000),
    made_on       DATE          NOT NULL
);
CREATE INDEX period_log_sheet ON period_log (sheet_id, period_id, id);

-- The sheet's today when a patron was named, and when a user started watching a person.
ALTER TABLE patron ADD COLUMN added_on DATE;
ALTER TABLE watch ADD COLUMN added_on DATE;

package net.officefloor.hq.app.claim;

import java.math.BigDecimal;
import java.time.LocalDate;

/**
 * A claim of a person on a sheet: an amount (two decimals; negative only for a correction), a date, a note (may be empty), its status
 * its number (given when opened; kept when voided; null for a draft) and its due fixed when settled (null when not
 * settled, or settled while its grade had no rate), who opened it (null when never opened),
 * whether it is bound to the figure it had at its person's last statement ({@code stated}) and that figure
 * ({@code statedDue}; null when it had none), and for a correction (a negative amount) the number of the SETTLED
 * claim of the same person it corrects ({@code corrects}; null for any other claim), and its due-by ({@code dueBy}), fixed
 * when it is added from its person's own terms, else those of their grade in force on its date (see SettingRepository#terms), and the
 * date it is deferred until ({@code deferredUntil}; null when never deferred; see ClaimDue#deferred), and its proofs
 * count ({@code proofs}; 0 when added, raised by one at a time; see ApplyProof), and for a claim split off another
 * the number of the claim it was split from ({@code splitFrom}; null for any other claim; see ApplySplit).
 */
public record Claim(long id, String sheetId, long personId, BigDecimal amount, LocalDate date, String note,
        ClaimStatus status, String number, BigDecimal due, String openedBy, boolean stated, BigDecimal statedDue,
        String corrects, LocalDate dueBy, LocalDate deferredUntil, int proofs,
        String splitFrom) {
}
package net.officefloor.hq.app.claim;

import java.time.LocalDate;
import java.util.List;

/** A claim as sent to the screen: the amount as text with two decimals, so it is never rounded through a float;
 *  the number is null when the claim has none; due is the due fixed when settled (two decimals), null while it is
 *  live; openedBy is who opened it, null when never opened; stated is whether it is bound to the figure statedDue
 *  (two decimals, null when it had none) by its person's last statement; corrects is the number of the claim a
 *  correction corrects (null for any other claim); roundsOn is the date that decides how its live figures round
 *  (the corrected claim's date for a correction, else its own; see Rounding); dueBy (yyyy-MM-dd) is its due-by, fixed
 *  when it was added; deferred is whether it is deferred on the sheet's today (see ClaimDue#deferred) and deferredUntil
 *  (yyyy-MM-dd) the date it was last deferred until (shown even once that date has passed), null when never deferred; proofs is its proofs count; splitFrom is the number of the claim it was split from (null for any other claim); log is its status log, oldest first: each status it has had, who made the change, the sheet's
 *  today (yyyy-MM-dd) then, and its due as shown at that moment (two decimals, or n/a); lockedBy is who has its editor
 *  open (null when no one does); lateEntry is whether it was added while its period was soft-closed. */
public record ClaimResponse(long id, String sheetId, long personId, String amount, String date, String note,
        String status, String number, String due, String openedBy, boolean stated, String statedDue, String corrects,
        String roundsOn, String dueBy, boolean deferred, String deferredUntil, int proofs, String splitFrom, List<LogLine> log,
        String lockedBy, boolean lateEntry) {

    /** One line of a claim's status log as sent to the screen. */
    public record LogLine(String status, String by, String date, String due) {
    }

    public static ClaimResponse from(Claim claim, ClaimRepository claims, ClaimLogRepository log, LocalDate today) {
        return from(claim, claims, log.of(claim.sheetId(), claim.id()), today);
    }

    public static ClaimResponse from(Claim claim, ClaimRepository claims, List<ClaimLogLine> log, LocalDate today) {
        return from(claim, claims, log, today, claims.lockedBy(claim.sheetId(), claim.id()),
                claims.lateEntry(claim.sheetId(), claim.id()));
    }

    public static ClaimResponse from(Claim claim, ClaimRepository claims, List<ClaimLogLine> log, LocalDate today, String lockedBy,
            boolean lateEntry) {
        boolean deferred = ClaimDue.deferred(claim, today);
        return new ClaimResponse(claim.id(), claim.sheetId(), claim.personId(), claim.amount().toPlainString(),
                claim.date().toString(), claim.note(), claim.status().name(), claim.number(),
                claim.due() == null ? null : claim.due().toPlainString(), claim.openedBy(), claim.stated(),
                claim.statedDue() == null ? null : claim.statedDue().toPlainString(), claim.corrects(),
                Rounding.roundsOn(claim, claims).toString(), claim.dueBy().toString(),
                deferred, claim.deferredUntil() == null ? null : claim.deferredUntil().toString(), claim.proofs(), claim.splitFrom(),
                log.stream().map((l) -> new LogLine(l.status().name(), l.by(), l.date().toString(), l.due())).toList(),
                lockedBy, lateEntry);
    }
}

content.text:
Claims can now be reminded, and all 4 tests in the spec pass with `bin/e2e`.

**Reminders**
- Each claim row has a Remind button (`claim-remind`) and shows its reminded date (`claim-reminded`). The date is the last day a reminder was written, or blank if there was none.
- A reminder goes through only for an OPEN or PENDING claim that hasn't already been reminded on the sheet's today. Otherwise the server refuses it (409), the row shows `claim-error`, and nothing is stored or audited. Viewers, archived sheets and as-of views are already refused by the existing `ViewerGuard`.
- The audit line follows the other claim lines: `REMIND sheet=… by=… person=… amount=… date=…`, plus `number=…` when the claim has one.
- Reminders are kept in a new table, `claim_reminder` (`V40__claim_reminder.sql`), with one row per claim per day. A unique constraint backs up the once-per-day rule. Because every day is kept, the as-of view shows the last reminder on or before the as-of date.
- The endpoint is `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/claims/{claimId}/remind`, built from four small steps (`ValidateRemind` → `LoadClaim` → `SaveReminder` → `RecordClaimReminded`).

**A fix outside the request.** Scenario 2 failed for a reason unrelated to reminders. Viewed as of 2026-03-15, a claim should show the amount and date it had then (20.00, 2026-02-25).
